On Friday, September 10, 2010 at 9:59:52 PM UTC+2 Dennis Murphy wrote:
> Hi:
>
> Here's an example with geom_segment(), similar to the last example on its help page:
>
> dat <- data.frame(k = 0:20, prob = dbinom(0:20, n = 20, p = 0.5))
> p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = k, y = prob))
> p + geom_segment(aes(xend = k, yend = 0)) + ylab('p(k)')
>
> To play with the width of the bars, try as an alternative
> p + geom_segment(aes(xend = k, yend = 0), size = 3) + ylab('p(k)')
>
> This produces the attachment.
>
> HTH,
> Dennis
>

messages.subject: How to reverse the order of a legend so as to have the lowest value at the top
messages.subject_clean: How to reverse the order of a legend so as to have the lowest value at the top
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
 I would really appreciate any help. How can I reverse the order of my legend so as to have the lowest value (ie 0 - 400) at the top and the highest value (  i.e > 2400) at the bottom. Here is a brief part of my script and my map in pdf.

library (ggplot2)

#Create a data frame from the raster
rdf <- as.data.frame(elevation_raster, xy=TRUE)
names(rdf)

##create the breaks on the raster
my_breaks <- c(400,800,1200,1600,2000, 2400,2794)

ggplot()  + geom_raster(data = rdf, aes(x,y, fill = layer)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = 1, na.value = 'white', name="Elevation", breaks = my_breaks , labels = c("0 - 400m ","400 - 800m", "800 - 1200m", "1200 - 1600m", "1600 - 2000m", "2000 - 2400m", "> 2400m"))

messages.subject: Re: How to reverse the order of a legend so as to have the lowest value at the top
messages.subject_clean: How to reverse the order of a legend so as to have the lowest value at the top
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

>  How can I reverse the order of my
> legend so as to have the lowest value (ie 0 - 400) at the top and the
> highest value (  i.e > 2400) at the bottom.

> ggplot()  + geom_raster(data = rdf, aes(x,y, fill = layer)) +
>    scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = 1, na.value = 'white',
> name="Elevation", breaks = my_breaks , labels = c("0 - 400m ","400 -
> 800m", "800 - 1200m", "1200 - 1600m", "1600 - 2000m", "2000 - 2400m", ">
> 2400m"))

Try adding the option:
guide = guide_colourbar(reverse = TRUE)
into your scale_fill_viridis_c call.

Hope this helps. I think it should do it, it worked on a very
simple example without the other options you have.

Ron.

messages.subject: Showing species occurrence points and a shapefile in a legend
messages.subject_clean: Showing species occurrence points and a shapefile in a legend
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I have plotted species occurrence points (blue triangles) in my map. I also have plotted the shapefile protected area in my map (in red dashed lines). How can I show these occurrence points and the protected area on my legend exactly as they appear in my map and even label them. Any help or leads on how to do this. I would really appreciate any leads to this.Attached is my map and brief code

ggplot()  +
  geom_raster(data = rdf, aes(x,y, fill = layer)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = 1, na.value = 'white', name="Elevation", breaks = my_breaks , guide = guide_colourbar(reverse = TRUE), labels = c("0 - 400m ","400 - 800m", "800 - 1200m", "1200 - 1600m", "1600 - 2000m", "2000 - 2400m", "> 2400m")) +  theme(legend.position = c(0.78, 0.55)) +
  geom_polygon(data=PA, aes(long, lat, group = group), colour = "red", size = 0.2, fill = 'white', alpha = .001, linetype="dashed")  + geom_point(data = occurence_data, aes(x = Lon, y = Lat), size = 2, shape = 23, fill = "blue", alpha = .5)
